parsed.g: Show the least expensive SSD hard drive with a minimum storage capacity of 1TB.
P_t: Searched for 'SSD 1TB' using the search bar, producing 504 results
Activated ascending price sort direction by clicking the direction-switcher link (URL now contains product_list_dir=asc)
R_t: Apply 'Price' as the sort-by field (currently still sorted by Relevance per the DOM select element)
Identify the least expensive standalone SSD hard drive with at least 1TB storage capacity from the sorted results
Navigate to or display that product
parsed.e_t: The page is the search results page for 'SSD 1TB' at http://172.185.52.29:7770/catalogsearch/result/index/?product_list_dir=asc&q=SSD+1TB. The URL includes product_list_dir=asc, meaning ascending direction is set, but the sort order field (select#sorter) still has 'relevance' selected (not 'price'). The current 12 products shown are not SSD hard drives — they are USB hubs, HDMI adapters, a CCTV DVR, a headphone amplifier, a storage bag, a security camera, a kids tablet, a laptop docking station, and a handheld gaming console, with prices ranging from $13.99 to $226.99. The Sort By dropdown shows 'Relevance' as selected. The direction link reads 'Set Descending Direction' (class sort-asc), confirming ascending direction is active. There are 504 total results across 42+ pages.
C: Must find a standalone SSD hard drive (not a computer or device that contains an SSD as a component)
Must identify the least expensive qualifying product

F_t.action: Clicked Sort By combobox [2782] at step 2 to open sort dropdown
F_t.cause: This opened the dropdown but did not apply any sort; the sort remained on Relevance per DOM

F_t.action: Clicked menuitem 'Price' [3032] at step 3 to sort by price
F_t.cause: Per DOM at step 4, the sort combobox still showed 'Relevance' as selected; clicking a menuitem in this UI did not apply the price sort

F_t.action: Clicked direction-switcher link [2783] 'Set Ascending Direction' at step 4
F_t.cause: This set the direction to ascending (URL now has product_list_dir=asc) but the sort field remained 'relevance' not 'price', so results are still sorted by relevance ascending, not price ascending
Per DOM at step 6, the sort select element still shows 'relevance' as selected; the price sort was not applied — the page reloaded with product_list_dir=asc but orderDefault=relevance still active

F_t.action: Clicked Sort By combobox [5839] at step 6 to open dropdown
F_t.cause: This is the action taken at step 6; the DOM shows the page is still sorted by relevance with ascending direction, and none of the 12 visible products are 1TB SSD hard drives

K_t: The search 'SSD 1TB' returns 504 results across multiple pages
The URL parameter product_list_dir=asc is active, meaning ascending direction is set
The sort order is still 'relevance' (not 'price') per the DOM select element — price sort has not been successfully applied
The toolbar config shows orderDefault=relevance and directionDefault=desc, meaning the default is relevance descending
To sort by price ascending, both the sort field must be changed to 'price' AND direction must be 'asc'

From the initial relevance-sorted results (steps 1-4), identified standalone 1TB SSD candidates: SK hynix Gold S31 1TB at $97.99, Crucial P2 1TB at $99.99, SanDisk 1TB Extreme PRO Portable External SSD at $299.99
The current page (price ascending by direction but relevance by order) shows non-SSD products priced from $13.99 to $226.99
The agent needs to successfully select 'Price' in the sort dropdown (select#sorter with data-role=sorter) to apply price sorting
